claims.text: The multilayer architecture creates a high density of coherent or semi-coherent interfaces.
Coherent or semi-coherent interfaces block and trap dislocations.
Compositional modulation enhances solid-solution strengthening.
Interface barriers and solid-solution strengthening impede dislocation glide and delay creep onset under sustained load.
Controlled deposition can establish coherent or semi-coherent interfaces between compositionally varied but compatible high-entropy-alloy layers.
A homogeneous coating with the same overall composition and thickness but without multilayer architecture can serve as the controlled baseline.
Prolonged constant-stress creep testing at 500–700 °C can be used to compare strain evolution in the multilayer and homogeneous coatings.
Abrupt compositional variations at interfaces produce local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions at the interfaces further resist plastic flow.
Under sustained elevated-temperature stress, dislocations in the multilayer coating pile up at interfaces rather than propagating freely.
Interface-mediated dislocation blocking and compositional strengthening reduce the effective creep rate relative to a homogeneous coating.
The multilayer coating will have a significantly lower steady-state creep strain rate than the homogeneous baseline.
The multilayer coating will show a delayed onset of plastic deformation relative to the homogeneous baseline.
In-situ characterization will show dislocation accumulation at multilayer interfaces.
The multilayer coating will accumulate less total strain over time than the homogeneous baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies when dislocation-mediated creep is dominant and interfacial coherence is maintained.
Extensive interdiffusion can undermine the interface-mediated creep resistance.
At sufficiently high temperatures or long durations, diffusion-driven interfacial degradation may reduce the multilayer benefit.
The magnitude of creep-rate reduction and interface stability may depend on layer thickness and compositional contrast.
Similar creep-strain evolution and dislocation behavior in the multilayer and homogeneous coatings would falsify the proposed mechanism.
